title: Guro Reiten joins Gotham FC from Chelsea
content:
Gotham FC has completed the signing of Norway international Guro Reiten from Chelsea.

Reiten, 31, has joined the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) side on an initial loan through to July, and has agreed to a free agent deal following the conclusion of her Chelsea contract this summer.

Gotham announced the winger has agreed a deal through to 2029 once her loan spell concludes.

“Gotham has built something special over the past few years, and there’s clear ambition here,” Reiten said in a press release. “I’m looking forward to working hard, learning and doing everything I can to help the team succeed.”

Reiten joined Chelsea from LSK Kvinner in the summer of 2019 and has been an integral part of the club’s success over the past six and half years.

She departs the club having scored 59 goals across 207 appearances, winning six Women’s Super League titles in the process. U.S. women’s national team head coach Emma Hayes, who signed Reiten for Chelsea, described the Norway international as “one of the best, a delight to coach”.

Hayes wrote on Instagram: “A wand of a left foot and an amazing person. You’ve got yourself a winner and a fantastic player”.

Reiten has made 17 appearances this season, scoring once, but has been limited to just three starts in the WSL. Chelsea are nine points off league leaders Manchester City, but remain in the Champions League and FA Cup, and face Manchester United in the League Cup final on Sunday.

“Guro is a player of exceptional quality who has consistently performed at the highest levels of the game,” Yael Averbuch West, general manager and head of soccer operations for Gotham FC, added. “Her experience competing for major trophies with Chelsea and her impact with the Norwegian national team will bring valuable leadership and attacking creativity to our squad.”

Gotham finished eighth in the NWSL last season to secure the division’s final playoff spot. The team went on to eliminate NWSL Shield winners Kansas City Current in the playoffs and before beating Washington Spirit to win the NWSL Championship.

Gotham start their 2026 NWSL title defense run on Saturday against expansion team Boston Legacy at Gillette Stadium.

Analysis from Melanie Anzidei

After a relatively quiet offseason, Gotham did what it does best: convince one of the best players in the world to call their club home.

After and a half years at Chelsea, Guro Reiten’s shock exit from the WSL proves Gotham is determined to win its third NWSL championship. The 31-year-old forward brings with her a winning track record and valuable experience to Gotham as they prepare for the long season ahead. Reiten’s versatility on the wing is invaluable as the NWSL side looks to deepen its already-impressive depth chart.

The club’s depth has essentially been their secret weapon, helping them navigate player injuries while also providing tactical options for head coach Juan Carlos Amoros, especially with more mid-week games in 2026.

Reiten’s creativity in attack will pair nicely with midfielders Jaedyn Shaw and Rose Lavelle, making Gotham an even more dangerous threat in the attacking third.

Reiten’s arrival means a reunion with ex-Chelsea teammates Jess Carter and Ann-Katrin Berger, a bonus as the Norwegian forward begins to acclimate to the NWSL. While Gotham says Reiten won’t be available for their season opener against Boston, her potential debut for their March 21 home opener comes as a surprise few saw coming, with four days still to go in this year’s primary transfer window.
